name: Learn: Scheduling
objective: CKA › Workloads & Scheduling. Drill EVERY way to control where pods land, harder than the exam: node labels + nodeSelector, taints & tolerations (Equal + Exists), required and preferred nodeAffinity, pod anti-affinity spread, manual nodeName scheduling, DaemonSet coverage, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix for an unschedulable pod. Graded exactly, per requirement.
description: Eight strict scheduling practicals on a 1-control-plane + 2-worker cluster. Each Check shows which requirements you met and the exact reason for any you missed.

questions.title: Label a node + nodeSelector
questions.teach:
`spec.nodeSelector` is the simplest placement control: the pod only lands on a node whose labels contain **every** key/value listed (exact equality, AND'ed). Label a node with `kubectl label node <node> key=value`.

**Gotcha:** if no node carries the label, the pod sits `Pending` forever — check `kubectl describe pod` events.
questions.prompt:
Worker node `$W1` exists. Label it `disktype=ssd`, then in namespace `sched-learn` create pod `ssd-pod` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`) with `nodeSelector` `disktype=ssd`.

Target: `ssd-pod` is `Running` and its `.spec.nodeName` is the node you labeled `disktype=ssd`.
questions.hint: `kubectl label node "$W1" disktype=ssd`, then set `spec.nodeSelector.disktype: ssd` on the pod.
questions.solution:
kubectl label node "$W1" disktype=ssd --overwrite
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: ssd-pod
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    disktype: ssd
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: ssd-pod Running on a disktype=ssd node via nodeSelector

questions.title: Taint a node + matching toleration
questions.teach:
A **taint** repels pods that don't tolerate it: `kubectl taint node <node> key=value:NoSchedule`. A pod opts in with a `toleration` whose `key`/`value`/`effect` match (operator `Equal`).

**Gotcha:** a toleration only *permits* the node, it doesn't *attract* — pair it with `nodeSelector`/affinity to actually land there.
questions.prompt:
Taint node `$W1` with `workload=batch:NoSchedule`. Then in `sched-learn` create pod `batch-pod` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`) that **tolerates** that taint (operator `Equal`) AND uses `nodeSelector disktype=ssd` so it lands on `$W1`.

Target: `$W1` carries the taint and `batch-pod` is `Running` on `$W1` with a matching toleration.
questions.hint: `kubectl taint node "$W1" workload=batch:NoSchedule`. Toleration `{key: workload, operator: Equal, value: batch, effect: NoSchedule}` plus `nodeSelector: {disktype: ssd}`.
questions.solution:
kubectl taint node "$W1" workload=batch:NoSchedule --overwrite
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: batch-pod
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    disktype: ssd
  tolerations:
  - key: workload
    operator: Equal
    value: batch
    effect: NoSchedule
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: $W1 tainted workload=batch:NoSchedule and batch-pod Running there with matching toleration

questions.title: Required nodeAffinity (In operator)
questions.teach:
**nodeAffinity** (`spec.affinity.nodeAffinity`) is a richer nodeSelector using `matchExpressions` with operators `In`, `NotIn`, `Exists`, `Gt`, `Lt`. The **hard** form `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` must be satisfied or the pod stays `Pending`.

**Gotcha:** affinity attracts but doesn't defeat taints — since `$W1` is now tainted, this pod also needs a toleration.
questions.prompt:
Node `$W1` is labeled `tier=gold`. In `sched-learn` create pod `affinity-pod` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`) using **required** nodeAffinity matching `tier In [gold]`, tolerating any taint so it can land on `$W1`.

Target: `affinity-pod` is `Running` on the `tier=gold` node via required nodeAffinity.
questions.hint: Under `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution.nodeSelectorTerms[0].matchExpressions[0]` set `key: tier`, `operator: In`, `values: [gold]`. Add `tolerations: [{operator: Exists}]`.
questions.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: affinity-pod
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        nodeSelectorTerms:
        - matchExpressions:
          - key: tier
            operator: In
            values: ["gold"]
  tolerations:
  - operator: Exists
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: affinity-pod Running on tier=gold node via required nodeAffinity

questions.title: Preferred nodeAffinity (soft, weighted)
questions.teach:
The **soft** form `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` is a *preference*, not a rule: each entry has a `weight` (1–100) and a `preference` term. The scheduler favors matching nodes but still schedules elsewhere if none match.

**Gotcha:** preferred affinity never leaves a pod `Pending` — if no node matches it just lands somewhere else, so you can't rely on it for a hard placement requirement.
questions.prompt:
In `sched-learn` create pod `prefer-pod` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`) that **prefers** (weight `80`) nodes labeled `zone=b`, tolerating any taint. Node `$W2` is labeled `zone=b`.

Target: `prefer-pod` is `Running` and declares a `preferredDuringScheduling` nodeAffinity entry of weight `80` matching `zone In [b]`.
questions.hint: `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: [{weight: 80, preference: {matchExpressions: [{key: zone, operator: In, values: [b]}]}}]`; add `tolerations: [{operator: Exists}]`.
questions.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: prefer-pod
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - weight: 80
        preference:
          matchExpressions:
          - key: zone
            operator: In
            values: ["b"]
  tolerations:
  - operator: Exists
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: prefer-pod Running with preferred nodeAffinity weight 80, zone In [b]

questions.title: Manual scheduling with nodeName
questions.teach:
Setting `spec.nodeName` directly **bypasses the scheduler** — the kubelet on that exact node picks the pod up and runs it. Use it to pin a pod deterministically or when the scheduler is unavailable.

**Gotcha:** a wrong/nonexistent node name does **not** error — the pod sits `Pending` with no scheduler event, since no scheduler ever looked at it.
questions.prompt:
In `sched-learn` create pod `manual-pod` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`) bound to worker `$W2` **via `spec.nodeName`** (no nodeSelector/affinity).

Target: `manual-pod` is `Running` and `.spec.nodeName` == `$W2`.
questions.hint: Put `nodeName: <the $W2 node name>` in `spec`. Find the exact name with `kubectl get nodes`.
questions.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: manual-pod
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  nodeName: $W2
  containers:
  - name: c
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: manual-pod Running and pinned to $W2 via nodeName

questions.title: DaemonSet on every node
questions.teach:
A **DaemonSet** runs one copy of a pod on every matching node, adding/removing as nodes join/leave. Like a Deployment but with no `replicas`, and `spec.selector.matchLabels` must match the template labels.

**Gotcha:** control-plane nodes (and your tainted `$W1`) carry `NoSchedule` taints — to cover *every* node the template needs `tolerations: [{operator: Exists}]`, which tolerates all taints.
questions.prompt:
In `sched-learn` create DaemonSet `node-agent` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`, label `app=node-agent`) with a toleration broad enough (`operator: Exists`) to run on **every** node including the control plane and the tainted `$W1`.

Target: `desiredNumberScheduled` == number of nodes and `numberReady` matches.
questions.hint: DaemonSet selector `app=node-agent`; template `tolerations: [{operator: Exists}]`. Verify with `kubectl -n sched-learn get ds node-agent` vs `kubectl get nodes`.
questions.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: node-agent
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: node-agent
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: node-agent
    spec:
      tolerations:
      - operator: Exists
      containers:
      - name: c
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: DaemonSet node-agent runs one ready pod on every node

questions.title: Pod anti-affinity (spread across nodes)
questions.teach:
**podAntiAffinity** keeps pods apart: the required form with `topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname` and a `labelSelector` matching the pod's own label forces replicas onto **different** nodes. The scheduler won't co-locate two matching pods on one host.

**Gotcha:** if replicas exceed available nodes, the extra pods stay `Pending` — hard anti-affinity can't double up on a host.
questions.prompt:
In `sched-learn` create a 2-replica Deployment `spread` (`busybox:1.36`, `sleep 3600`, pod label `app=spread`) with **required** podAntiAffinity on `topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname` matching `app=spread`, tolerating any taint.

Target: both `spread` replicas are `Running` on **different** nodes via required podAntiAffinity.
questions.hint: `affinity.podAntiAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: [{labelSelector: {matchLabels: {app: spread}}, topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname}]`; add `tolerations: [{operator: Exists}]` so both nodes are usable.
questions.solution:
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: spread
  namespace: sched-learn
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: spread
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: spread
    spec:
      tolerations:
      - operator: Exists
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
          - labelSelector:
              matchLabels:
                app: spread
            topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
      containers:
      - name: c
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sleep","3600"]
EOF

verification.description: spread: 2 replicas Running on 2 distinct nodes via required podAntiAffinity

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a pod that won't schedule
questions.teach:
A pod stuck `Pending` with **no node assigned** is a scheduling failure — run `kubectl describe pod

` and read **Events**: `0/N nodes are available` names the reason (a nodeSelector/affinity that matches nothing, or a taint with no toleration). **Gotcha:** fix the **Deployment template**, not the pod — the ReplicaSet recreates the pod, then confirm with `kubectl rollout status`.
questions.prompt:
Deployment `sched-diag` in `sched-learn` shows `0/1` — its pod is `Pending` and never schedules. Diagnose the scheduling fault and fix it so the Deployment reports an available replica. Don't delete and rebuild from scratch — find and fix what's wrong.

Target: Deployment `sched-diag` has at least 1 available replica.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n sched-learn describe pod -l app=sched-diag` → the events say no node matches its `nodeSelector` (disktype=nvme). Either remove that nodeSelector or point it at a label a node actually has, then watch `rollout status`.
questions.solution:
# describe shows: 0/3 nodes available — node(s) didn't match nodeSelector disktype=nvme.
# No node has disktype=nvme, so remove the impossible selector (an untainted node will take it).
kubectl -n sched-learn patch deployment sched-diag --type=json \
  -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/spec/nodeSelector"}]'
kubectl -n sched-learn rollout status deployment/sched-diag

verification.description: Deployment sched-diag has >=1 available replica (scheduling fault fixed)
